The ancestor conventions split every topic into a normative markdown spec and a rendered HTML view, and kept both current in the same commit. But the owner reviews only the rendered views, so the spec layer was a second file per topic that its one reader never opened. Therefore this directory holds self-contained HTML documents only, and a decision is recorded as a dated principle document such as this one.

The decision

Every document in docs/ is one reviewable .html file. There is no specification layer beside it; what must stay true is carried by dated principle documents, and the normative home for workspace rules remains .claude/CLAUDE.md.

The unread layer was pure cost

A spec that is never read cannot catch drift, and it still charges its maintenance on every change: two files edited per topic, and a "which one lost" judgment on every disagreement. The one reader reviews rendered pages; the cost had no buyer.

A dated decision record cannot go stale

A spec that mirrors an artifact is wrong after the artifact's next change. A decision with its date and reasons records what was decided then, which no later commit can falsify — so the record layer that remains is the one layer that does not rot.

One self-contained file survives every host

A view with inline styles and no network dependency opens from file://, from git history, and from whatever serves it next. Nothing about review depends on tooling staying alive.

Options considered

Axes: review bandwidth, staleness risk, cost per change.

OptionWhat it doesWhy it lost
Two layersmarkdown spec plus HTML view per topicdoubles cost per change to serve a reader who does not exist here
Generated viewsrender HTML from the specs by scriptadds a build the documents must never depend on to open
Views only (chosen)one HTML document per topic; decisions as principle records—
